system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Each state in the ASM other than the ‘ done’ state is associated with a unique prompt template. Prompt templates are filled with information from the local KG subgraph and the KG interface before presenting them to the LLM.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: a local KG subgraph is initialized to contain the entities present in the original query. It is then expanded using a tree search algorithm to choose actions and thoughts generated by an LLM
env_context_strategy.note: Environment is a knowledge graph explored via Select_Entities/Select_Relation actions; initial seeding of query entities is a mild up-front injection.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: Local KG subgraph is represented using a a token efficient YAML format that minimizes repeti-tion for multiple edges on the same entity.
context_compaction.note: No compaction mechanism described; the paper notes context window as a limitation instead.

observation_format.evidence_quote: Local KG subgraph is represented using a a token efficient YAML format

tool_call_format.note: Actions are emitted as constrained text lines (e.g. 'ANSWER: <answer>', 'EXPAND_KG', selections); closest value is text-embedded structured action, not native function calling.

tool_count.evidence_quote: a finite state ma-chine with the following actions: Think, Answer, ExpandKG, Select_Entities, and Select_Relation

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: Tree-of-Traversals can be used forK as long as the following interfaces are implemented.
edit_primitive.note: No file editing; actions only query KGs.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: A customized prompt for each state allows us to present precise and relevant information along with specific instructions for each state to the LLM
tool_schema_source.note: Prompt templates authored by hand (Appendix F.1-F.3).

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: This interface is implemented with SPARQL queries when available; otherwise, we use the graph API that is available for the KG.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: a tree search algorithm which defines the overall LLM search trajectory such as best first search, backtrack upon making a mistake, and termination condition when an answer is found
loop_primitives.note: Default is tree search (k=3) over thought/action nodes; k=1 (Chain-of-Traversals) is a ReAct-like chain.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: From the default state, Tree-of-Traversals can either Think, Answer, or choose to ExpandKG.
planning_granularity.note: No stored plan object; planning only via free-text Think actions.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: Tree-of-Traversals is a powerful algorithm that en-ables LLMs to utilize KG reasoning with zero examples

delegation_mechanism.note: Single LLM sampled for actions and values; no agent delegation.

human_in_loop.note: Fully automatic loop; no human gate in Algorithm 1.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: The Tree-of-Traversals algorithm maintains a local KG subgraph that is repeatedly expanded until it contains all the information required by an LLM to answer the given query.
short_term_state.note: State is a search-tree node with local KG subgraph, action state, and value.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: Tree-of-Traversals is a powerful algorithm that en-ables LLMs to utilize KG reasoning with zero examples, no schema dependency, and no train-ing.
long_term_memory.note: External KGs are read-only knowledge sources, not cross-run agent memory.

self_verification.evidence_quote: This value is created by the LLM using eval-uation prompts (step evaluate in Algorithm 1). The value can be between 0 to 1 where 1 indicates highest utility.
self_verification.note: Same model self-evaluates node/answer values; could also be read as self_critique.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: The search stops when an answer is found with a node value exceed-ing the threshold τ.
retry_policy.note: Re-sampling/backtracking continues until an answer passes the value threshold, capped by max expansions (20).

rollback.evidence_quote: the model backtracks to the best alternative state.
rollback.note: Backtracking in the search tree, not rollback of environment changes (no mutations made).

termination_condition.evidence_quote: max depth of the tree search, after which the algorithm is forced to transition to the done state (i.e., answer the query), and max expansions after which the model halts exploration and returns "Cannot find answer".
termination_condition.note: Answer action with value > τ is the model-declared stop; depth 7 and 20 expansions are the caps.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: However, compared to non-retrieval baselines, there is significant increase in token usage cost.
cost_controls.note: Expansion caps bound cost implicitly but no token/cost budget mechanism described.

timeouts.evidence_quote: To bound the search space we add two hyper-parameters: max depth of the tree search
timeouts.note: Only iteration caps; no timeouts reported.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: This interface is implemented with SPARQL queries when available; otherwise, we use the graph API that is available for the KG.
execution_isolation.note: Actions execute as remote KG API/SPARQL calls (Wikidata, MusicBrainz) from the host process.

filesystem_access.note: KG interface only reads; no write operations. Coded relative to the KG environment.

network_policy.evidence_quote: we implement the KG in-terface for MusicBrainz KG using the MusicBrainz API
network_policy.note: Outbound calls to public APIs; no egress restriction described.

permission_model.evidence_quote: an action state machine (ASM) which is a finite state machine that defines the fea-sible space of actions, states, and prompt templates
permission_model.note: The ASM restricts which actions are legal in each state; closest to a static allowlist.

tracing.evidence_quote: The prompts include the original query, the local KG subgraph, the trajectory of previous actions
tracing.note: A search tree with per-node actions and values is maintained; explicit logging facilities not described.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: Evaluation of Tree-of-Traversals on two ques-tion answering tasks: 2WikiMultiHop and QALD-10 and comparison with baselines.
eval_hooks.note: Paper evaluates on benchmarks and releases code plus a new dataset; runner presence in repo not verified from evidence.

guardrails.evidence_quote: the LLM does not know what relations are available in the graph or what relations are valid for a given entity
guardrails.note: Constrained sampling over KG-provided options prevents invalid actions.

target_domain.evidence_quote: a novel zero-shot reasoning algorithm that enables augmentation of black-box LLMs with one or more KGs
target_domain.note: Domain is knowledge-graph question answering; closest values are research/knowledge tasks with structured tool interfaces.

open_source.evidence_quote: Code is available at https: //github.com/amazon-science/ tree-of-traversals

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: We evaluate Tree-of-Traversals using three differ-ent models available on Amazon Bedrock
model_agnostic.note: Black-box LLM access; Claude-Instant, Llama2-70b, Llama2-13b.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: Code is available at https: //github.com/amazon-science/ tree-of-traversals
primary_artifact.note: Coded from the paper; repo not inspected at a pinned commit.

first_release_date.note: Basis: arXiv v1 date; no tag information available.
